_comment: Generalization/regularization domain term/alias map for EXT-009 cross-vault candidate discovery (CAP-013). Canonical term -> aliases. Built from the actual content of batch 008 (master-ai '03 - Machine Learning/Generalization' — 01 Bias Variance Tradeoff + 06 Regularization Techniques, 2 files, 106 KUs) and batch 009 (ai-course '04.3 - Training Dynamics and Stability' files 05 Batch Normalization + 06 Dropout and Regularization + 07 Data Augmentation — the regularization-relevant subset of that folder, 3 of 7 files, 234 KUs; three deterministic single-file runs concatenated in fixed order); every term and alias is verified to occur inside at least one in-scope KU excerpt by scripts/ext009_term_map.py after two probe rounds (scripts/ext009_term_probe{,2}.py; reports/extraction/ext009-term-map-verification.json). HEADING-ONLY vocabulary correctly EXCLUDED (EXT-004 rule: headings are not KU-excerpt evidence): 'lasso' and 'weight tying' exist only as master-ai section headings ('### L1 (Lasso)', '## Weight Tying') and never inside a KU excerpt; 'scikit-learn', 'smoothness', 'test-time augmentation', 'drop rate', 'drop probability', 'inference mode', 'coadaptation', 'augment', 'language model', 'fine-tune' are absent from both batches. BRIDGE aliases deliberately connect different surface forms of the same concept across vaults: 'batchnorm' (cross-vault compound) with 'batch norm' (master-ai) and 'BN' (ai-course); 'test set' (master-ai) with 'test data' (ai-course); 'hyperparameter' (ai-course) with 'hyperparameters' (master-ai); 'regularize' (master-ai) with 'regularized' (ai-course). KNOWN SPURIOUS/SENSE-COLLISION SOURCES, recorded here so classification dismisses or adjudicates them with evidence: (1) 'noise' — master-ai uses it for irreducible noise, noise injection, and batch-statistics noise; ai-course for Gaussian-noise augmentation; (2) 'translation'/'shift' — ai-course geometric transformations vs master-ai 'back-translation' (text augmentation) and 'pitch shift' (audio augmentation) — both sides ARE augmentation senses but of different operations; (3) 'scaling' — dropout/inverted-dropout scaling (both vaults) vs master-ai 'Scaling Laws' pretraining link; (4) 'L1'/'L2' — occur in one mermaid diagram (KU-8612af2c187e43bf) and in python code blocks; CAP-013 mermaid-node-suspect flagging and code-fence handling apply (F-0006); (5) 'bias'/'variance' — statistical senses (master-ai core) vs BN parameter names 'beta'/'gamma' and batch variance (ai-course); (6) 'inference' — dropout-at-inference (master-ai pitfall list) vs LLM inference contexts. Keys starting with _ are documentation and ignored by the loader.
